name: Cementerio de San Fernando — Pico Reja mass grave, Seville
story: General Gonzalo Queipo de Llano seized Seville on 18 July 1936, crushing working-class resistance in Triana and La Macarena and broadcasting nightly radio speeches from Unión Radio that threatened opponents with death. The repression that followed killed thousands in the city. Many were buried in Pico Reja, a mass grave in the municipal cemetery of San Fernando. Among them is probably Blas Infante, the 'father of Andalusian nationalism', shot on 11 August 1936 at km 4 of the Carmona road. Excavations begun in 2020 are one of the largest in Spain.
see: The municipal cemetery with the excavated Pico Reja area and memorial markers; the exhumation site itself may be fenced.
plan: Cemetery open daily; ask at the entrance for the Pico Reja area. For Infante, his house in Coria del Río is now the Museum of Andalusian Autonomy.

boxes.text: Number of dead in Pico Reja and of Seville's repression overall is disputed; identification of Infante's remains had not been confirmed at time of writing.
